question: When was the First Five-Year Plan of India launched?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1951**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The First Five-Year Plan of India was launched in **1951**.
 
• This plan was based on the Harrod-Domar model and focused on the agricultural sector, aiming to improve food production and address the scarcity of food grains.
 
• It aimed at the overall development of agriculture, irrigation, and power sectors, emphasizing the importance of community development projects.
 
• The plan was successful in achieving its targets, especially in the agricultural sector, which saw significant growth during this period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of Five-Year Plans in India was inspired by the Soviet model of planned economy.
 
• The Planning Commission of India was established in 1950 to oversee the implementation and formulation of the Five-Year Plans.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan laid the foundation for the subsequent plans and set the precedent for planned economic development in India.
 
• The success of the First Five-Year Plan encouraged the government to continue with the planned approach to economic development.
